title: Netanyahu's nuclear image, two days before Israel votes

scenes.title: Netanyahu's nuclear image, two days before Israel votes
scenes.say: Two days before Israel votes, Benjamin Netanyahu posted a mushroom cloud over Tel Aviv. Here's why.

scenes.title: An AI-generated image of a nuclear blast over Tel Aviv
scenes.say: On 25 October, the Israeli prime minister shared an AI-generated image of a nuclear explosion engulfing the city.
scenes.speak: On the twenty-fifth of October, the Israeli prime minister shared an AI-generated image of a nuclear explosion engulfing the city.

scenes.text: The State of Israel is in real and tangible existential danger.
scenes.role: Israeli writer and commentator, in the statement Netanyahu shared
scenes.say: With it came a statement by commentator Yuval Blumberg: Israel is in real and tangible existential danger if Iran gets nuclear weapons.

scenes.label: of Trump's term left to 'finish the work in Iran', the statement argued
scenes.say: Its argument: Israel has two more years of Donald Trump to finish the work in Iran, and no one knows what comes after.
scenes.speak: Its argument: Israel has two more years of Donald Trump to finish the work in Iran, and no one knows what comes after.

scenes.text: The man and those around him have lost it. The pressure is mounting.
scenes.say: Rivals called it fearmongering. Yair Golan said Netanyahu should be kept off social media. Gadi Eisenkot called him hysterical.

scenes.title: Israel votes on Tuesday
scenes.say: Israel votes on Tuesday by proportional representation. A party or coalition needs 61 of the Knesset's 120 seats to govern.
scenes.speak: Israel votes on Tuesday by proportional representation. A party or coalition needs sixty-one of the Knesset's hundred and twenty seats to govern.

scenes.title: Iran, Israel and the oil route
scenes.say: For India, a two-year deadline on Iran means risk. Most of India's crude is imported, and much of the Gulf's energy passes through Hormuz.

scenes.title: What escalation could cost
scenes.say: Escalation could mean higher oil, freight and insurance costs, a weaker rupee, and a harder balancing act between Israel, Iran and the Gulf.
